clue.text: Rise awkwardly to position of defiance

indicators.note: done awkwardly, the word rise is set out in a clumsy new order

parts.note: a stance is a position, the way one stands

explanation.surface: Someone stands up clumsily to take a defiant stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'position of defiance' reads as one phrase, but the split falls after 'position'; 'awkwardly' makes RESI.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: opposition to authority or force is defiance.

parts.note: E for East, standard crossword shorthand for oriental

parts.note: to couple is to mate, pair up

explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a noun (children, a topic) but is the verb: to flow out.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to issue is to flow out or proceed from a source.

clue.text: One type of wood is the best

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: A claim that one particular timber beats all others.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect standard or model, the very best one can imagine.

clue.text: Exchange rate certain to provide wealth

indicators.note: to exchange is to swap round, so the letters of rate trade places

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A financial claim that a currency rate is a guaranteed money-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchange rate' is a single financial term on the surface; 'Exchange' alone signals the jumble, making TREA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: accumulated riches or valuables, a hoard of money.

clue.text: Lacking reputation despite anything to the contrary

parts.note: lacking something is being not with it
standing is one's status or reputation

explanation.surface: A person with no good name pressing on regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: A preposition or adverb meaning in spite of something, nevertheless.

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' reads as passing a test; it is the verb for time going by.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses passes or slips by.

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.definitionFit: A flat floating platform is a simple kind of boat or craft.

explanation.definitionFit: Getting something back, the act of recovering it.

parts.note: florid means ruddy, red-faced

parts.note: to put away food is to eat it; ate is the past tense

explanation.surface: A man banked his money and stored his fortune.

indicators.note: crashed planes are wrecked, so the letters of the word are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
spirit is strong alcoholic drink

to sear is to burn, as when cauterising a wound
CH is Companion of Honour, a British award

explanation.surface: Army medics burning a comrade's wound while under inquiry.

clue.text: One dispatches journalist supporting one-time president

parts.note: ex means former, one-time

definitions.meaning: people who break into computer systems are known by this name

clue.text: Caught part of face a blow

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

clue.text: Hates the French adopting bad language

clue.text: Ploughman keeps time for a novel

parts.note: a tiller is someone who tills the soil

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ploughman' suggests Piers Plowman or a lunch; a tiller is simply one who tills the soil.

clue.text: Caught after no ball when cutting

explanation.definitionFit: A cutting from a newspaper is a passage taken out of it.

clue.text: Look into crash in obstacle race

parts.note: slam means crash or bang

parts.note: a comet travels through space

clue.text: Travel a short time to the river

Elaine is a girl's name
